conventions.players: P1 and P2. first_player is given per case (default P1). 'lineup' = whose lineup the card came from (never changes); 'controller' = who holds it now.
conventions.slots: a1-a3 (row A, top), b1-b4 (row B), c1-c3 (row C, bottom). Rows A and C are offset half a brick inward.
conventions.values: Card values are printed Top/Side/Bottom from the cards table; effective_values include placement bonuses.
conventions.fixtures: Boards are rule-isolation fixtures and need not be reachable in a legal game (see RQ-18). Build them with a test helper that sets cells, controllers, face-down flags, Signature flags and Cipher active traits directly.
conventions.springs: springs_after lists start-of-turn springs for the next player triggered when the turn passes after this step, or all pending springs in placement order when the wall becomes full. Their captures are not part of 'captured'.
conventions.controllers_after: Full map of occupied slots to controller after the step and its springs.
conventions.score_after: Score after the step (and springs), same function as final scoring.
conventions.cipher: A placed Cipher card's active trait is what it copied; 'none' when nothing was copied. Board entries for Cipher cards carry active_trait.
conventions.error_codes: Suggested names; tests may map them to the engine's enum.

rules_questions.question: Cipher: how long does a copied trait last?
rules_questions.context: Spec 4.4 says Cipher copies a trait on placement, and 10 has a copied Ambush spring a turn later, so the copy outlives the placement. It doesn't say whether a copied Steady keeps protecting the card.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: The copied trait replaces Cipher for the rest of the match, wherever the card is and whoever controls it. A copied Steady keeps protecting it.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Cipher copying a Cipher card that has already copied something
rules_questions.context: Spec 10 says "Cipher copying Cipher: no trait". It doesn't say whether that means the target's printed trait (Cipher) or the trait it holds now.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Copy the printed trait. Copying any Cipher card gives no trait, even if it holds a copied one.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Cipher: what may be picked, and is copying optional?
rules_questions.context: "one adjacent card (your pick)" doesn't say whether the card can be an enemy's, a face-down Ambush or a traitless card, or whether the player can decline.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Any adjacent card of either side, face-down included (only Ambush cards go face-down, so that trait is public). Picking a traitless or Cipher card gives no trait, which is how a player opts out. place() takes a required copy_from slot whenever the card has a neighbour.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Cipher holding a copied Ambush: capture before the spring, and last placement
rules_questions.context: Spec 10 says it stays face-up, so it can be captured before it springs. It doesn't say what happens to the spring then, or what happens on the last placement.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: If the placer no longer controls it when their next turn starts, the spring is cancelled. On the last placement it springs right away before scoring, like a real Ambush.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Ambush spring and placement bonuses
rules_questions.context: Spec 4.3.3 limits Set Link and Clutch to "the placed card's comparisons on that turn". A spring happens on a later turn.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: A spring uses printed values +1 (ambush_spring_bonus) only. No Set Link, no Clutch, no Veteran (the card's trait is Ambush). Steady still applies. Springs never chain unless chain_captures is on.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Order of resolution inside one placement
rules_questions.context: Reclaim, Set Link and captures all happen "on placement", and the order changes results (see the Reclaim cases).
rules_questions.proposed_answer: 1) Cipher copy. 2) Bonuses (Set Link, Clutch) read from the board before anything flips. 3) Reclaim. 4) Value captures against enemy-controlled, face-up neighbours. 5) Chain, if on. 6) Turn passes, and the next player's springs resolve (or all pending springs, in placement order, if the wall is full). 7) Scoring.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Set Link: what counts as "your own cards"?
rules_questions.context: It could mean cards you control now, or cards from your lineup.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Cards you control at that moment, including captured enemy cards. Your lineup cards held by the enemy don't count. Note: your own face-down card never exists on your own turn, because it springs at the start of it.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Do the two Showcase cards get Set Link with each other?
rules_questions.context: Spec 6 gives Chrome Tiger and Gold Leaf the set "Showcase", and Set Link applies to "all cards". But the binding anti-pay-to-win rule says store cards never get more power.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Yes. Set Link isn't a trait, and it gives the same +1 every set gets, so it isn't extra power. Needs a design call: if store cards should get no bonus at all, exclude the Showcase set and flip the expectation in that case.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Clutch "behind" check: which score?
rules_questions.context: Spec 10 says "current score before placement, with Signatures counted double". It doesn't mention face-down cards, Triptychs, or springs that happen at the start of the turn.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Use the same score function as end-of-game scoring (Triptych bonus included), on the true board: face-down cards count for their owner, Signature included. Take it after this turn's start-of-turn springs. "Behind" means strictly lower. UI note: if a face-down card is the Signature, the score counter would reveal it, so the UI should show face-down cards as 1 point plus a "?".
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Is a Reclaim retake a "capture"?
rules_questions.context: It matters for "Carded!", the Dead Air unlock ("capture 20 cards total") and the placement preview.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: No. It's a separate "reclaim" event: no "Carded!" and no capture count. The preview shows it with its own marker.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: When exactly does "Carded!" play?
rules_questions.context: Spec 4.5 says "capturing an enemy Signature".
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Whenever a Signature from the opponent's lineup comes under your control through a value capture, a spring or a chain, and again each time this happens. Never for retaking your own Signature, whether by capture or by Reclaim.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Triptych ownership and counting
rules_questions.context: "three of your cards" could mean cards you control or cards from your lineup. It's also open whether order matters and whether a player can score more than one.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Cards you control at the end, from either lineup, in any order, in a run of 3 consecutive slots of one row (A: a1-a3, B: b1-b3 or b2-b4, C: c1-c3). Each Triptych scores at most once per player, and different Triptychs add up. The "first time revealed" reward belongs to the collection and only fires for the human player.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: What happens when chain captures are turned on?
rules_questions.context: Spec 9 only says "captured cards re-check their neighbors".
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Breadth-first. Each newly captured card attacks its enemy-controlled, face-up neighbours with printed values and its own trait (Veteran ties count, Steady blocks, no Set Link or Clutch). Reclaimed cards don't chain. Default stays off.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Can values go above 9?
rules_questions.context: Values are 1-9, but bonuses can push past 9 (Polar Night: Side 10 with Clutch and Set Link).
rules_questions.proposed_answer: No cap. Compare integers.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Lineup: duplicates, Showcase limits, Signature
rules_questions.context: The brief asks for store-card limits, but the spec sets none. It also doesn't say whether duplicates are allowed.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: No duplicates. No limit on Showcase cards, since they're already Clearance 1 with no trait. Exactly one Signature, chosen from the 5, and a Showcase card may be it. The two players may bring the same card (rival lineups are fixed), so the engine must track card instances, not card ids.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: When is the loaner lineup offered?
rules_questions.context: Spec 4.2 says "if their collection can't make a full 5".
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Offer it when the collection can't form any legal lineup (5 distinct owned cards, Clearance cap, Legend limit). A collection of 5 owned Clearance-3 cards counts as "can't".
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Spec 8 walkthrough contradicts Clutch
rules_questions.context: Step 4 says the player is "behind 3-4" and then Archivist plays Polar Night with Clutch +2. Archivist is ahead, so Clutch can't fire.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Fix the walkthrough text: Archivist is behind, so make it "ahead 4-3", or drop the Clutch mention. The rule itself stays.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Isolated test boards
rules_questions.context: Many cases use boards that can't come up in a legal game (for example one side has more cards than turns played). That keeps each rule isolated.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: The engine's test helper (WallState.from_setup) must accept any board with explicit to_move and first_player fields. Cases that model the end of a game use reachable boards (5 cards per lineup).
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Hidden information in face-down cards
rules_questions.context: Hand order is hidden and Ambush cards are face-down, but lineups are public.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: The AI and the preview may know a face-down card is an Ambush, but not which card it is. Only the engine's springs and scoring use its identity.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: What does the placement preview cover?
rules_questions.context: Spec 11 asks for a preview of "which cards would flip". It doesn't say whether that includes the springs that follow.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: The placed card's own resolution only: captures, reclaims, copied trait and bonuses, plus its own immediate spring if this placement fills the wall. Never the opponent's pending springs.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

cases.title: Full adjacency table of the 3-4-3 brick wall
cases.rationale: Every slot's neighbours and the facing direction from that slot. Row A sits on row B, row C hangs under row B; rows A and C never touch.

cases.title: Neighbour counts, symmetry and edges
cases.rationale: b2 and b3 have 6 neighbours; a2 and c2 have 4; a1, a3, c1, c3, b1, b4 have 3. Adjacency is symmetric, 19 edges in total, no wrap-around, and no row-A slot touches a row-C slot.

cases.title: b1 touches exactly one card above (a1) and one below (c1)
cases.rationale: Mayday T5 S5 B5. a1 Gold Leaf: Top 5 vs Bottom 4, captured. c1 Glacier: Bottom 5 vs Top 7, no. b2 Service Ribbon: Side 5 vs 5, tie, no. a2 and c2 are not adjacent to b1 and are never compared.

cases.title: b4 touches exactly one card above (a3) and one below (c3)
cases.rationale: Brass Tacks T6 S6 B5. a3 Service Ribbon B4 < 6, captured; b3 Chrome Tiger S4 < 6, captured; c3 Glacier T7 > 5, no. a2/c2 not adjacent.

cases.title: Corner a1: one side neighbour and two below
cases.rationale: a1 compares Side vs a2, and Bottom vs the Top of b1 and b2. a2 S5 < 6 and b1 T4 < 5 are captured; b2 Flare Up (face-up) T6 > 5 holds. c1 and b3 are not neighbours of a1.

cases.title: Row C attacks upward with its Top value
cases.rationale: c2's above-neighbours are b2 and b3: placed Top 5 vs their Bottom 4, both captured. Sides: c1 Glacier S2 captured, c3 Brass Tacks S6 holds. b1 is not adjacent to c2.

cases.title: Defender's facing value is the side pointing back at the placed card
cases.rationale: vs a2 (above): Top 5 vs Chrome Tiger's Bottom 4, captured (using its Top 5 would wrongly tie). vs c3 (below): Bottom 5 vs Flare Up's Top 6, no (using its Bottom 4 would wrongly capture). vs b4: Side 5 vs 6, no.

cases.title: No wrap-around: a3 does not touch a1, b1 or c3
cases.rationale: a3 neighbours are a2, b3, b4 only. a2 S5 < 6 captured; b3 Top 4 < Bottom 5 captured; b4 Top 5 = Bottom 5, tie, no.

cases.title: Corner c3: all three neighbours captured
cases.rationale: c3 touches c2 (side) and b3, b4 (above). Top 5 vs Bottom 4 twice and Side 5 vs 4: all captured. c1 and a3 are untouched.

cases.title: Ties do nothing in every direction
cases.rationale: Top 5 vs Neon Rain B5, Side 5 vs Gold Leaf S5, Bottom 5 vs Graveyard Shift T5: all ties, no capture. Only b3 (S4) is captured.

cases.title: A placed card is never captured by its neighbours
cases.rationale: Only the placed card attacks. Gold Leaf T4 S5 B4 loses every comparison; nothing flips, and b2 stays with P1.

cases.title: Own neighbours are never compared (no friendly fire)
cases.rationale: a1, b1, c1 are P1's and stay P1's. b3 Frostbite S6 vs 6, tie. c2 Open Channel T4 < Bottom 5, captured. No Old Guard neighbour, so no Set Link.

cases.title: Multi-capture sweep from b2
cases.rationale: Top 6 vs B4, B4; Side 6 vs S4 (b1) and S6 (b3, tie); Bottom 5 vs T4 (c2). Four captures in one placement.

cases.title: Chain captures OFF (default): captured cards do not re-check
cases.rationale: Brass Tacks captures b3 Chrome Tiger (S4 < 6). Chrome Tiger would beat b4 Glacier (S4 > S2) and c3 Frostbite (B4 > T3), but with the flag off nothing cascades.

cases.title: Chain captures ON (tuning flag): captured cards re-check their neighbours
cases.rationale: Proposed chain semantics: b3 Chrome Tiger, now P1's, attacks with printed values: Side 4 > Glacier S2 (b4) and Bottom 4 > Frostbite T3 (c3, Steady C1 is not higher than Chrome Tiger's C1). The cascade stops when no new card flips.

cases.title: Captured cards can be recaptured by values
cases.rationale: Control is not permanent. P2's Mayday S5 beats Chrome Tiger S4 (currently P1's), so it flips back to P2.

cases.title: A captured card keeps its trait for its new controller
cases.rationale: Brass Tacks (Steady, C3) now belongs to P1 and still can't be captured by Neon Rain (C2), even though S6 vs S6 is a tie Veteran would win. c3 Gold Leaf T4 < Bottom 5 is captured.

cases.title: Steady blocks a lower-Clearance attacker that wins on values
cases.rationale: Glacier (C2) Top 7 beats Brass Tacks Bottom 5, but Brass Tacks is Steady with C3 > 2: no capture. b1 Gold Leaf B4 < 7 is captured.

cases.title: Steady does not block an equal-Clearance attacker
cases.rationale: Gold Leaf (C1) Bottom 4 vs Frostbite Top 3. Frostbite is Steady C1; the attacker's C1 is not lower, so it is captured.

cases.title: Steady does not block a higher-Clearance attacker
cases.rationale: Brass Tacks (C3) Side 6 vs Mayday (Steady, C2) Side 5: captured.

cases.title: Placement bonuses never raise Clearance
cases.rationale: P1 is behind 0-3, so Open Channel's Clutch gives 6/7/8. Side 7 beats Brass Tacks S6, but Open Channel is still C2 < C3: Steady holds. a1 Gold Leaf B4 < 6 is captured.

cases.title: Veteran captures on ties
cases.rationale: Service Ribbon T4 S5 B4. b3 S5 = 5 and a1 B4 = T4 are ties: captured (Veteran). c1 Graveyard Shift T5 > Bottom 4: no.

cases.title: Veteran tie vs an equal-Clearance Steady card captures
cases.rationale: Neon Rain (C2) Bottom 5 vs Mayday Top 5: tie, Veteran wins, and Mayday's Steady (C2) does not protect against C2. a1 Glacier B6 > Top 4: no.

cases.title: Ambush is placed face-down and captures nothing
cases.rationale: Snow Blind would beat both neighbours (S5 > 4, T6 > 4), but a face-down card captures nothing on placement.

cases.title: A face-down card can't be captured
cases.rationale: Dead Air Side 8 would beat Snow Blind S5, but b2 is face-down: no comparison. c2 Gold Leaf T4 < Bottom 5 is captured. When P1's turn starts, Snow Blind springs at 7/6/7: Side 6 < Dead Air S8, Bottom 7 > Gold Leaf T4, so c2 comes back.

cases.title: Spring at the start of the owner's next turn with +1 to all values
cases.rationale: Last Train 6/4/5 springs as 7/5/6 when P1's turn starts. Top 7 > Glacier B6 and Side 5 > Chrome Tiger S4: both captured. Without the +1 both would be ties. b3 was placed after the Ambush; the spring checks the neighbours present when it springs.

cases.title: Spring respects Steady, and spring ties do nothing
cases.rationale: Flare Up springs as 7/4/5 (C1). a1 Mayday: Top 7 > B5 but Steady C2 > 1, blocked. b1 Chrome Tiger: Side 4 = 4, tie, no. c1 Gold Leaf: Bottom 5 > T4, captured.

cases.title: Set Link does not apply to a spring
cases.rationale: Last Train springs as 7/5/6. It touches own Graveyard Shift (Night Shift), but Set Link is a placement bonus: Side 5 vs Mayday S5 is a tie, no capture. (With Set Link it would be 6 > 5.)

cases.title: Ambush on the last placement springs immediately before scoring
cases.rationale: The 10th placement fills the wall, so Flare Up springs at once (7/4/5, C1): b3 Service Ribbon B4 < 7 captured; b2 Brass Tacks B5 < 7 but Steady C3 blocks; c3 Neon Rain S6 > 4. Score P1 5 (a1, a2 x2, b2, c3) vs P2 7 (a3, b1, b3, b4, c1 x2, c2).

cases.title: An earlier Ambush still face-down when the wall fills flips before scoring
cases.rationale: P2's 10th placement (Frostbite) takes c2 Glacier (S6 > S2) and can't touch face-down b3. The wall is full, so Last Train springs (7/5/6): a2 and a3 (B4 < 7) and c3 Frostbite (T3 < 6, Steady C1 < C2 doesn't block) are captured; b2 S5 = 5 tie; c2 Glacier T7 > 6 holds.

cases.title: Ambush next to Ambush: the face-down one is safe from the spring
cases.rationale: P1's Last Train springs first (7/5/6). Its Side 5 would beat Flare Up S3, but b3 is still face-down, so nothing. On P2's next turn Flare Up springs (7/4/5): a2 Gold Leaf B4 < 7 captured; b2 Last Train (now face-up) S4 = 4, tie.

cases.title: Two Ambushes pending at wall fill resolve in placement order
cases.rationale: Placement 9 (P1) springs first: Last Train 7/5/6 takes a2 (B4) and b1 (S4); b3 is face-down; c2 Glacier T7 > 6. Then Snow Blind 7/6/7 springs: takes Last Train (S4 < 6), a2 back (B4 < 7), a3 Brass Tacks (B5 < 7; Steady C3 is not higher than C3) and c3 Service Ribbon (T4 < 7).

cases.title: A spring that takes the enemy Signature plays "Carded!"
cases.rationale: Last Train springs (Side 5 > Chrome Tiger S4) and takes P2's Signature: Carded! P1 scores b2 + b3 x2 = 3.

cases.title: Reclaim retakes adjacent own-lineup cards whatever the values; normal captures still apply
cases.rationale: City Never Sleeps (7/5/7) takes back a1 and b1 (its own lineup's cards held by P2), including P1's own Signature (no Carded: it's P1's own). It also captures a2 Dead Air (B5 < 7). b3 Honor Roll S6 > 5; c1 Glacier T7 = 7 tie. a3 is P1's card but not adjacent: it stays with P2.

cases.title: Bonuses are fixed before Reclaim: a reclaimed card doesn't give Set Link
cases.rationale: Graveyard Shift (Night Shift) is enemy-held when City Never Sleeps lands, so no Set Link; Bottom 7 vs Glacier T7 is a tie. (If Reclaim resolved first, Set Link would make it 8 > 7.)

cases.title: Reclaim beats Steady (via Cipher copying Reclaim)
cases.rationale: Null Glyph (C2) copies Honor Roll's Reclaim and takes back Brass Tacks (Steady, C3), even though C2 < C3. c1 Frostbite T3 < Bottom 5 is captured; a2 Honor Roll B6 > Top 5 holds.

cases.title: Clutch +2 when behind
cases.rationale: P2 is behind 1-3. Open Channel fights as 6/7/8: Top 6 > Graveyard Shift B4 and > Mayday B5 (Steady C2 doesn't block C2). Without Clutch both would fail.

cases.title: Clutch is off when the score is level
cases.rationale: 2-2 is not behind. Top 4 vs B4 is a tie and 4 < 5.

cases.title: Clutch is off when ahead
cases.rationale: P2 leads 2-1. Open Channel plays at printed values: Top 4 vs Graveyard Shift B4 is a tie.

cases.title: Behind-check counts Signatures double (behind on points, level on cards)
cases.rationale: Two cards each, but P1's Signature makes it 3-2: P2 is behind, Clutch applies, and taking Mayday (P1's Signature) plays Carded!

cases.title: Behind-check counts Signatures double (fewer cards but level on points)
cases.rationale: P2 has 2 cards vs 3, but its Signature makes it 3-3: not behind, no Clutch.

cases.title: Clutch and Set Link stack (+3)
cases.rationale: Polar Night (Whiteout) touches own Glacier (Whiteout) and P2 is behind 1-3: 5/7/5 becomes 8/10/8. Top 8 > City Never Sleeps B7 needs both bonuses (+2 alone gives a tie).

cases.title: Clutch applies to the placement only; later it defends with printed values
cases.rationale: Next turn Service Ribbon's Side 5 ties Open Channel's printed S5 (not 7) and Gold Leaf S5: both captured by Veteran. a2 Mayday (now P2's) B5 > Top 4 holds.

cases.title: Behind-check is taken after own start-of-turn springs
cases.rationale: P1 trails 1-3 until Last Train springs and takes b3, making it 2-2. Open Channel then gets no Clutch: Top 4 vs Gold Leaf B4 tie, Bottom 6 vs Glacier T7. (With the pre-spring score it would have taken both.)

cases.title: Face-down cards count in the behind-check
cases.rationale: P1's face-down Flare Up counts, so P2 is behind 1-2: Top 6 > Graveyard Shift B4. Then P1's turn starts and Flare Up springs (Top 7 > Gold Leaf B4).

cases.title: Cipher copies Veteran (player's pick) and captures on ties
cases.rationale: Null Glyph 5/5/5 ties all four neighbours (B5, S5, S5, T5). As a Veteran it takes all of them; Mayday's Steady (C2) doesn't block C2.

cases.title: The pick matters: copying Steady instead captures nothing
cases.rationale: Same board as the previous case; Null Glyph copies Mayday's Steady. All four comparisons are ties.

cases.title: A copied Steady keeps protecting the Cipher card
cases.rationale: Frostbite (C1) Side 6 beats Null Glyph S5, but Null Glyph copied Steady earlier and is C2: blocked.

cases.title: Cipher copies Clutch while behind
cases.rationale: P1 is behind 0-4. Key Fragment 6/5/6 copies Open Channel's Clutch: 8/7/8. Glacier B6, Open Channel S5 and Honor Roll T5 fall; Polar Night S7 = 7 is a tie.

cases.title: Cipher copying Ambush: stays face-up, captures nothing, springs next turn with +1
cases.rationale: Null Glyph would take Chrome Tiger (S5 > 4) but captures nothing on placement. On P1's next turn it springs as 6/6/6: Chrome Tiger S4 captured; Snow Blind B6 = Top 6, tie.

cases.title: A Cipher holding a copied Ambush can be captured before it springs
cases.rationale: Null Glyph is face-up, so Glacier (Top 7 vs B5) captures it. Proposed: its pending spring is cancelled because P1 no longer controls it.

cases.title: Cipher copying a Cipher card gets no trait
cases.rationale: Key Fragment copies Null Glyph's trait, Cipher, which gives no trait. Side 5 vs 5 is a plain tie; a1 Service Ribbon B4 < Top 6 is captured.

cases.title: Copying a Cipher that copied something still gives no trait
cases.rationale: Null Glyph currently holds Veteran, but its printed trait is Cipher, so Key Fragment gets nothing and Side 5 vs 5 doesn't capture.

cases.title: Cipher with no neighbours gets no trait, and later neighbours don't add one
cases.rationale: No neighbour at placement, so no trait. Frostbite (C1) Side 6 > 5 captures it; nothing protects it.

cases.title: Copying a traitless Showcase card gives no trait
cases.rationale: Gold Leaf has no trait to copy. Side 5 = 5 and Bottom 5 = Chrome Tiger T5 are ties.

cases.title: Cipher copying Ambush on the last placement springs immediately
cases.rationale: Null Glyph copies the (face-up) Last Train's Ambush. It's the last placement, so it springs before scoring as 6/6/6: b3 Last Train B5 < 6 captured; b2 Brass Tacks blocked by Steady (C3 > C2); c3 Neon Rain S6 = 6 tie.

cases.title: Cipher may copy a face-down Ambush
cases.rationale: Only Ambush cards go face-down, so the trait is public. Null Glyph captures nothing (it would have taken b1). When P2's turn starts, Flare Up springs (Side 4 < Null Glyph S5): nothing.

cases.title: Set Link +1 when touching an own same-set card
cases.rationale: Frostbite (Whiteout) touches own Glacier: 4/7/5. Side 7 > Honor Roll S6 and Bottom 5 > Service Ribbon T4, which are ties or losses without the bonus. c1 Chrome Tiger T5 = 5, tie.

cases.title: An enemy same-set card gives no Set Link
cases.rationale: Glacier is P2's. Frostbite fights at 3/6/4: every comparison is a tie or a loss.

cases.title: A non-adjacent own same-set card gives no Set Link
cases.rationale: a3 does not touch b2.

cases.title: Several same-set neighbours still give only +1
cases.rationale: Two Whiteout neighbours, one bonus. Top 4 vs Gold Leaf B4 is a tie, so a2 stays with P2 (a stacked +2 would wrongly take it).

cases.title: A captured enemy card of the same set gives Set Link to its new controller
cases.rationale: Proposed: "your own cards" means cards you control now. Same result as the basic Set Link case.

cases.title: Set Link applies to the placement only; later it defends with printed values
cases.rationale: Gold Leaf Bottom 4 vs Frostbite's printed Top 3 (not 4): captured (Steady C1 vs C1 doesn't block). Side 5 > Glacier S2. b3 Honor Roll T5 > 4 holds.

cases.title: Two Showcase cards link like any set
cases.rationale: Proposed: Set Link is not a trait, so Chrome Tiger next to own Gold Leaf gets +1. Side 5 > Graveyard Shift S4 (equal C1, Steady doesn't block).

cases.title: Capturing the enemy Signature plays "Carded!" and moves its 2 points
cases.rationale: Side 6 > Chrome Tiger S4 (P2's Signature) and Top 6 > Gold Leaf B4. P1 scores b2 + a1 + b3 x2 = 4.

cases.title: Recapturing your own Signature is not "Carded!"
cases.rationale: Mayday is P1's own Signature held by P2; taking it back scores 2 for P1 but is no Carded! moment.

cases.title: "Carded!" plays again each time the enemy Signature is taken
cases.rationale: P1 takes it (Carded!), P2 takes its own Signature back (no Carded), P1's Brass Tacks Top 6 takes Dead Air (B5) and Chrome Tiger (B4) again (Carded! again).

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: 1 point per card, Signature 2
cases.rationale: P1 controls a1, a3 (Signature, 2), b1, b2, c2, c3 = 7. P2 controls a2, b3, b4, c1 (Signature, 2) = 5. Points always total 12 without Triptychs.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Tie goes to the first player (P1 first)
cases.rationale: 6-6. Default flag: first player wins.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Tie goes to the first player (P2 first)
cases.rationale: Same board, P2 won the coin flip: P2 wins the tie. The rule follows the first player, not the P1 label.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Tie flag set to draw
cases.rationale: With tie_winner = draw, 6-6 is a draw.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Both Signatures held by one player both count double
cases.rationale: P1 holds its own Signature (a3) and P2's (c1): 2 + 2 + four single cards = 8.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Signature value tuning flag (3)
cases.rationale: Signatures worth 3: P1 5 cards + 3 = 8; P2 3 cards + 3 = 6.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Triptych +1: three cards in one row, any order
cases.rationale: Row C holds Neon Rain, Last Train, Graveyard Shift (Midnight Run), all P1's: 6 + 1 = 7. P2: 6.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Triptych in row B (b2-b4) counts
cases.rationale: b2, b3, b4 are consecutive in row B.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Not consecutive (b1, b2, b4): no Triptych
cases.rationale: b3 breaks the run. 6-6, P1 (first player) wins the tie.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: One Triptych card held by the opponent: no bonus for anyone
cases.rationale: P2 controls Last Train in c2, so neither player has all three.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: A column is not a row: no Triptych
cases.rationale: a1, b1, c1 form a column (they're adjacent bricks), not three consecutive slots of one row.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Triptych built partly from captured enemy cards counts
cases.rationale: Row A: Frostbite + Mayday + Dead Air (Cold Signal), all controlled by P1 at the end. 8 + 1 = 9.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Triptych bonus breaks a tie against the first player
cases.rationale: 6-6 on cards, P2's Midnight Run makes it 6-7: P2 wins although P1 went first.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Triptych bonus flag 0
cases.rationale: Same board with the bonus at 0: 6-6, first player wins.

cases.section: Scoring, Triptychs and the tie flag (spec 4.5)
cases.title: Two different Triptychs for one player
cases.rationale: Row A is Cold Signal and row C is Midnight Run: 8 + 2 = 10.

cases.title: The walkthrough lineup is legal (Clearance 10)
cases.rationale: 1+2+2+3+2 = 10 <= 12, no Legend, one Signature, all owned at demo start.

cases.title: Exactly 12 with one Legend is legal
cases.rationale: 4+3+2+2+1 = 12. The cap is inclusive.

cases.title: Clearance 13 is rejected
Two Legends are rejected even under the cap
cases.rationale: 4+4+1+1+1 = 11 <= 12, but at most one Legend (Clearance 4).

cases.title: Four cards are rejected
cases.rationale: Lineup size is exactly 5.

cases.title: Six cards are rejected
No Signature is rejected
cases.rationale: Exactly one Signature.

cases.title: Two Signatures are rejected
cases.rationale: Exactly one Signature.

cases.title: The Signature must be one of the 5 cards
cases.rationale: Snow Blind isn't in the lineup.

cases.title: The same card twice is rejected
cases.rationale: The collection holds one copy of each card.

cases.title: Showcase cards are legal and not limited in number
cases.rationale: Store cards are already Clearance 1 with no trait (Decision 3); proposed: no extra cap. Total 5. A Showcase card may be the Signature.

cases.title: Cards not in the collection are rejected
cases.rationale: Polar Night is locked at demo start. 1+2+2+3+2 = 10, otherwise legal.

cases.title: Loaner lineup is offered when the collection can't make a legal 5
cases.rationale: 4 cards can't make a lineup. The loaner lineup offered must itself pass validation.

cases.title: Loaner lineup is not forced on the demo start collection
cases.rationale: 13 owned cards make many legal lineups.

cases.title: Card data rules: budgets and the anti-pay-to-win rule
cases.rationale: All 20 demo cards have T+S+B = 13/15/17/19 for Clearance 1/2/3/4. Any Showcase (store) card must be Clearance 1 with trait none: a Showcase card with Clearance 2, or with a trait, fails validation. 13 cards are owned at demo start.

cases.title: Illegal placements are rejected and change nothing
cases.rationale: P2's hand is FRB, GLA, PNT, OCH, SRB. Each attempt returns an error code (names are suggestions) and the state is unchanged.

cases.title: Coin flip, strict alternation, 5 placements each, then the game is over
cases.rationale: With a fixed seed the coin flip is repeatable, and both outcomes occur across seeds. The first player makes placements 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; the other makes 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. After the 10th the state reports game over, and any further placement is rejected (GAME_OVER).

cases.title: preview() returns exactly what place() does
cases.rationale: For every placement step in this file, preview(state, card, slot[, copy]) returns the same captured and reclaimed slots, bonuses, copied trait and face-down flag as place(). Start-of-turn springs that follow are reported separately. Never preview the opponent's pending face-down cards (RQ-20).

expect.rule: for every placement step in kind placement/sequence: preview(state_before, card, slot, cipher_copy_from) == the placement part of place() (captured, reclaimed, set_link, clutch, effective_values, active_trait, face_down)

cases.title: Spec 4.6 worked example
cases.rationale: Neon Rain touches own Graveyard Shift (Night Shift): 5/7/6. a1 Glacier B6 > 5, no. b3 Mayday S5 < 7, captured (Steady C2 doesn't block C2). c2 Frostbite T3 < 6, captured (Steady C1). a2 and b1 empty. 2 captures.

cases.title: Worked example variant: 5 vs 5 captures because Veteran wins ties
cases.rationale: The spec's aside: with a defender Bottom of 5 (Mayday, C2), Top 5 vs 5 is a tie and Veteran captures.

cases.title: Scripted full duel (walkthrough lineup vs a 9-Clearance rival)
cases.rationale: An end-to-end script touching captures, Steady, Ambush springs, Clutch and a Steady block of a Veteran tie (move 10: Service Ribbon S5 = Mayday S5, but Mayday is C2 > C1). Final 7-5.
